correctness.rationale: A direct argument classifies every cohesive static approval group: mixed groups with a cross-approver automatically meet PJR/EJR/EJR+, while the two pure blocs impose the exact floor quotas. The binomial finite sum follows, the derivative identity proves a unique finite optimizer or explicit endpoint case, Stirling/large-deviations prove fixed-size regimes, and the de Moivre-Laplace CLT plus atom bound/Chebyshev prove the complete quadratic window. A standard-library checker directly evaluated all three axiom definitions on 6,858 small cases, compared exact rational probabilities, and checked numeric critical-window values: 7,758 finite checks and four numeric limit examples passed. These are auxiliary to the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The central gap is how often an uncoordinated i.i.d. temporal decision process meets demanding collective representation axioms ex post, as distinct from the existence of fair, adaptively constructed schedules. A single voter approving both candidates changes a one- or two-count feasible corridor to a macroscopic corridor; its impact is quantified by the unique optimal stationary bias, an exact Cramér failure exponent and a sharp Gaussian critical window at L comparable to n². This determines a natural boundary between dependence essential for ex-post fairness and independent sampling that becomes reliable; it is more substantive than renaming the binomial distribution.
